title: OSS entry points must construct QueryClient via the shared factory, not new QueryClient()
answers: why does the app use createMlflowQueryClient instead of new QueryClient
where should I create the react-query client in MLflow UI
new QueryClient in bootstrap.tsx or app.tsx causes offline hang
body:
Invariant: each OSS entry point builds its QueryClient with createMlflowQueryClient(), not a bare new QueryClient(). The factory carries the networkMode 'always' default.
Enforced at: shared/web-shared/query-client/createMlflowQueryClient.ts:createMlflowQueryClient, used by app.tsx:MLFlowRoot and oss-notebook-renderer/bootstrap.tsx:AppComponent.
What breaks if skipped: a bare client reintroduces the paused-query hang for that entry point; the notebook trace explorer hung identically before the factory was shared, because it used its own bare client over the same React Query instance.
Constraint: the eslint no-singleton-query-client suppression is placed on the factory's new QueryClient line, so new call sites should use the factory rather than add their own suppression.
applies: Any new OSS QueryClient creation under mlflow/server/js/src (app shell, notebook renderer, tests that mirror production wiring).
says: The notebook trace explorer hangs indefinitely and never finishes loading
Model trace view freezes inside the notebook when viewing traces offline
Queries in the user interface pause and hang without an active internet connection
Prevent the model trace viewer component from freezing when running in disconnected environments
search: Open-source entry points under mlflow/server/js/src must construct their QueryClient using createMlflowQueryClient rather than a bare new QueryClient(). Used by app.tsx:MLFlowRoot and oss-notebook-renderer/bootstrap.tsx:AppComponent, this factory enforces the networkMode 'always' default to avoid paused-query hangs when offline. The eslint no-singleton-query-client suppression belongs solely on the factory constructor line, so call sites must not add individual suppressions.
